status_summary: Force Design continues under the Commandant's 2025 Force Design Update, released 2025-10-23, which according to Military Times creates a Maritime Reconnaissance Company, treats the two Marine Littoral Regiments already in III MEF as the intended composition, and keeps 4th Marine Regiment as a reinforced infantry regiment instead of converting it into a third littoral regiment. For the light amphibious ship, P.L. 119-21 provides 160 million dollars in advance procurement and about 1.8 billion dollars for Landing Ship Medium procurement, Sec. 127 of the FY2026 NDAA authorizes a block buy of up to 15, and CRS reports the Navy selected the LST-100 design in December 2025, with construction expected from late 2026 and first delivery wanted by 2029. Federal law (10 U.S.C. 8062) requires a Navy force structure of not less than 31 larger amphibious ships, and the 381-ship plan described by CRS includes 18 LSMs against a Marine Corps goal of 35. No source was found on E-6 squad leaders, specific divestments or the current count of large amphibious ships.

timeline.event: Reconciliation law P.L. 119-21 enacted; per CRS its Sec. 20002 provides 160 million dollars in advance procurement and about 1.8 billion dollars for Landing Ship Medium procurement.
Commandant issues the 2025 Force Design Update.

Military Times reports the update creates a Maritime Reconnaissance Company, keeps the two Marine Littoral Regiments already in III MEF, and drops the plan to convert 4th Marine Regiment into a third.
FY2026 NDAA signed; its Sec. 127 covers procurement authorities for Medium Landing Ships, which CRS says allow a block buy of up to 15.
CRS reports the Navy selected the LST-100 design from Damen in December 2025, with construction expected from late 2026 and first delivery by 2029.

title: Marine Corps: continue Force Design 2030, light amphibious ships, 28 to 31 large amphibs
uncertainties: Force Design 2030 began before 2025 and this record covers actions since 2025-01-20 only, so the stage reflects continuation rather than new action on most items. The 2025 update itself was not read; Sea Power gives the release date as 2025-10-23 while Military Times says early October, and neither discusses divestments or NCO rank. E-6 squad leaders were not found in any source. The statutory floor of 31 larger amphibious ships predates the review period. The count of large amphibious ships and the amphibious content of the May 2026 shipbuilding plan were not retrieved. The LSM funding total adds CRS's two figures.
